summary.intent: Merge origin/main into the phase-44 branch (feat/ipns-conflict-handling), ship it as a PR, and resolve any CI failures or review comments that arose.
summary.outcome: Successfully merged 28 conflicts (taking main's reviewed phase-42/43 code wholesale), created PR #488, fixed two CI failures (stale test assertion + malformed commit messages via filter-branch rewrite), resolved 2 CodeRabbit threads, and confirmed the PR merged to main with all required checks green.

repo: Web app vitest only picks up `*.test.ts` files — `*.spec.ts` are silently skipped. NestJS API uses `.spec.ts` by convention (and those run), but web/sdk test files must be `*.test.ts`.
This repo uses `Entire-Checkpoint:` commit trailers, not `gate_status:` trailers — a TDD audit table populated from `gate_status:` would be all-missing rows.
PR titles must follow conventional-commit format enforced by `pr-title.yml` CI; the GSD template's literal `Phase N: name` title would have been rejected.
Repo is squash-only with PR_TITLE as the squash-commit subject, so the conventional PR title (not branch history) is what lands on main.
`required_signatures: false` — history rewrites without re-signing are allowed on this repo.
The Release Preview required check enforces conventional-commit format on every commit (excluding merges) that touches a versioned package; violations exit 1 and block merge.
Release Preview pushes a `chore(release): set release targets for PR #N` commit to the branch after a successful run — always fetch before pushing to avoid non-fast-forward.
1Password SSH signing hangs in sandbox; git commits require unsandboxed bash. `--no-gpg-sign` is not an option (signatures are enforced).
The gsd commit helper has a known false-negative: reports `commit_failed` but the commit actually lands — verify with `git log` rather than retrying.
Phase-44 code is isolated to `packages/sdk-core/`, `packages/sdk/`, and `apps/web/src/hooks/` — no overlap with the phase-42/43 Rust/API/desktop files.

code.finding: fetchQuota() is fire-and-forget (void + .then only); it warns on resolved-falsy with a single logger.warn arg and has no .catch — a rejection is silently swallowed, never logged.

mockPrivateKey was declared once at describe scope without beforeEach reinit; updateFileMetadata zeroizes it in-place (file/index.ts:399), leaving all-zero bytes for every subsequent test in the suite.
params.fileIpnsPrivateKey.fill(0) zeroizes the caller's buffer in-place after use — any test sharing a key reference across cases will see zeros after the first invocation.

Comment confirms: updateFileMetadata now publishes internally with CAS; the separate batchPublishIpnsRecords call was deliberately removed from updateSharedFile to avoid double-publish. Tests asserting the old direct call are stale.
main's guardedUnpin is a strict refinement of the branch's earlier cut: adds suppressCrossUserAudit option and inline lock computation. The branch's version was the pre-PR-review draft.

workflow: When merging branches with parallel feature implementations, determine which conflicted files the current branch's unique work actually touched before choosing a resolution strategy — if zero overlap, taking the other side wholesale is safe.
git filter-branch with --msg-filter can fix commit messages without touching tree content; verify the rewrite is message-only by diffing tree bytes before force-pushing.
Bundle related fixes (test fix + commit message rewrite) into a single push to minimize CI cycles.

For Release Preview failures, weigh `release:none` (kills all version bumps for the PR) vs a history rewrite (preserves releases but requires force-push) — rewrite is almost always correct for a real feature branch.
Delegating verbose build verification (pnpm typecheck, cargo check --workspace) to a sub-agent keeps the main context focused and returns only pass/fail + errors.
When a CodeRabbit comment targets a test file, always check whether that file actually runs in CI before patching the assertion — a dead duplicate is better deleted than fixed.
Fetch before every push when a bot (Release Preview, release-please) may have pushed to the branch between your last pull and your push.

friction: Transient git index.lock collision on two files (crates/fuse/src/commands/sync.rs, crates/fuse/src/fuse/mod.rs) during bulk `git checkout --theirs` — caused by a file watcher, resolved on retry after confirming lock was gone.
git filter-repo was not installed; had to fall back to the deprecated git filter-branch for the commit message rewrite.

28 merge conflicts arose because phases 42 and 43 were implemented independently on both the feature branch (sequentially) and their own PR branches that had already merged to main — a structural branching issue, not a one-off.
Phase-44 verification ran sdk-core (196/196) but not the full packages/sdk suite, so the stale batchPublishIpnsRecords assertion in shared-write.test.ts only surfaced in CI after the PR was created.
The gsd commit helper false-negative required an extra git log verification step after every commit to confirm the commit actually landed.

CodeRabbit suggested patching the assertion in the dead delete.service.spec.ts rather than identifying it as a stale duplicate — required manual investigation to find the canonical .test.ts and choose deletion over patching.
open_items: Three TODOs filed to .planning/todos/pending during phase-44 work: folder writes leak baseChildren/publishedChildren bookkeeping; unify file and folder IPNS CAS retry into one publishWithCas helper; updateSharedFile discards prunedCids from updateFileMetadata.

filter-branch backup refs (refs/original/…) remain locally after the commit message rewrite — harmless but can be cleaned up with `git update-ref -d refs/original/refs/heads/feat/ipns-conflict-handling`.
/gsd:complete-milestone has not been run yet — STATE.md already marks v1.1 milestone complete, but the GSD workflow step was noted as the suggested next command.
release-please will cut version bumps for packages/sdk-core, packages/sdk, and apps/web once PR #488 is processed — release PR not yet created at end of session.
